ledger.enumeration_rule: Every JSON mapping entry whose key matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+)+$ and contains no ":" and whose value matches ^[0-9a-f]{64}$. The manifest inventory is the git-tracked set at the checkout head (git ls-files) with the .json extension matched case-insensitively (22 tracked manifests use .JSON and are retained; a working-tree glob or a case-sensitive *.json query drops them and reports 17503 instead of 17525), excluding .git, .worktrees and this package. Shape L: member "files" whose value is such a mapping (check_sources-style live pin). Shape R-input and R-provenance: member "files" whose value is a list of path/usage/git_blob/sha256 records (research_package.py pins); for that validator only usage=="input" rows are checked against live working bytes ("working source drift"), usage=="provenance" rows bind historical blobs. Shape P: any other such entry (e.g. a catalogue digest recorded at task draw). Shapes are syntactic categories, not consumer semantics: the audit has not established per entry whether a consumer compares it to live bytes, and at least scripts/verify_pr_reconciliation.py:207 (ledger["source_sha256"]) and scripts/verify_replay_coverage.py:98 (selected["source_sha256"]) hash current bytes for some P-shaped entries. Classification of live pins is against the bytes a checker reads at the pinned path; other keys are counted ignored.
